newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers prepare to expand Hebron enclave.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers prepare to expand Hebron enclave.

text.p: Jewish settlers in Hebron dug foundations on Thursday in preparation for the expansion of an enclave in the Israeli-ruled part of the West Bank town, witnesses said.

David Wilder, a spokesman for the 400 Jews who live or study in Hebron, said they planned to construct apartments for about 10 families and that building permits had either been issued or promised by Israeli authorities.
Witnesses said about 50 settlers used pickaxes and shovels to dig holes in the ground near the Avraham Avinu enclave in the Old City of Hebron.
"That's something that has started a few weeks ago, to build an apartment building," Wilder told Reuters.

The settlers also cleared rubble from a nearby abandoned Arab building which Palestinians want to renovate, the witnesses said. Palestinians speculated the settlers planned to take over the structure.
"We have agreements with the Israelis on Hebron. But every day we get complaints (from Palestinians) that settlers are intruding on their property," said Hebron mayor Mustafa Natsheh.
Under a U.S.-brokered deal, Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO rule on January 17.
The accord gives Israel the authority to approve construction by Jewish settlers on land they own in the 20 percent of Hebron under Israeli control.

Khaled al-Qawasmi, an engineer with Hebron's Committee for Renovating the Old City which is spearheading repairs to old Arab houses in the city, said the work being carried out by the settlers threatened the foundations of Arab houses.
"The Palestinian side has complained to the Israeli side about the work. But the Israelis say that the settlers are only cleaning up," Qawasmi told Reuters.
"The other day, they prevented us from renovating Arab houses. But today they are letting settlers work unhindered," he said.

On Monday, Palestinians said Israeli police detained 11 men working in the old city of Hebron after military authorities delivered an order signed by West bank military commander Major General Uzi Dayan prohibiting the work. The army called it a security measure to protect Jewish settlers.
